title: Think Again
author: Adam Grant
blurb: Organizational psychologist Adam Grant argues that in a fast-changing world, the ability to rethink and unlearn matters more than raw intelligence. Most of us slip into three mental modes. We preach to defend our beliefs, prosecute to prove others wrong, and politick to win approval. Grant urges us to think like scientists instead, treating our opinions as hypotheses to test. He explores confident humility, the surprising joy of discovering we were wrong, and why healthy disagreement about ideas makes teams smarter. He then turns outward, showing how to open other minds through curious questions and genuine listening rather than force. Finally, he looks at building schools and workplaces where rethinking is safe, and at revisiting our own life plans before they become traps.

lessons.b: We often defend, attack, or seek approval for our views, but thinking like a scientist means treating beliefs as hypotheses to test.
The best thinkers pair belief in their ability to learn with humility about whether they currently have the right answer.
Detaching your identity from your opinions lets you enjoy discovering mistakes, because each one means you've learned something.
issues: scene 4: The figure's arm sticks out into empty space. The 'AN OPINION' bubble floats far away in the upper right, faint and tilted, and its tail points at nothing. The drawing reads as broken rather than as a person holding an opinion, which is what the narration ('something you hold') describes. (fix: Place the opinion card at the end of the arm so the hand visibly holds it, or draw a clear held-then-released path. Give it full-opacity indigo so it reads as intentional.)

scene 1: The 'WELDED' and 'MY OPINION' labels are tiny, roughly 14-16px at 1600 width, which is below the readability minimum. (fix: Increase these labels to at least 18-20px and give the zigzag weld more room if needed.)
scene 5: The 'DISTANT STAR' label is very small, roughly 14-16px at 1600 width. (fix: Raise it to at least 18px, matching the other mono labels such as 'A MISTAKE IN THE MATH'.)

lessons.b: Disagreement about tasks and ideas makes groups smarter, as long as it doesn't turn into personal conflict.
issues: scene 4: The indigo X marks sit directly on top of the 'A' and 'B' letters inside the two cards. The letters become nearly illegible, so the viewer cannot tell which position each brother held before it was crossed out. (fix: Show the letter clearly first, then strike it with a thinner diagonal line or a smaller X in a corner of the card. Alternatively, dim the letter to grey with a single strike-through so it stays readable.)

lessons.t: Debate Like a Dance, Not a War
lessons.b: Skilled persuaders find common ground, use a few strong arguments, and ask questions instead of overwhelming people with force.
